blocks.text: The Rh system is the second most important human blood group system. Its name comes from the Rhesus monkey, in which its antigen was first discovered by Landsteiner; the book dates this to the 1930s, and the discovery is usually credited to Landsteiner and Wiener in 1940. The system is based on the presence or absence of the Rh antigen, also called the Rh factor or antigen-D: people with it are Rh-positive and people without it are Rh-negative.

A blood group usually names both systems together: a person with antigen-A and the Rh antigen is A-positive, and one with antigen-A but no Rh antigen is A-negative; groups B, AB and O are named the same way.
Inheritance of the Rh blood groups
The gene D has two alleles: the dominant D forms the Rh antigen, and the book describes the recessive d as inhibiting its formation; in other words a dd person makes no Rh antigen.

blocks.alt: A table of the four ABO groups. Group A: genotype IA IA or IA i, square A antigens on the red cell, anti-B antibody. Group B: IB IB or IB i, triangular B antigens, anti-A. Group AB: IA IB, both antigens, no antibody. Group O: i i, no antigen, anti-A and anti-B. Below: DD or Dd is Rh-positive, dd Rh-negative; O-negative is the universal donor and AB-positive the universal recipient.
blocks.caption: The Rh rows and the universal donor and recipient (original diagram after Figure 18.5).
blocks.long_description: The I gene on chromosome 9 has three alleles: IA makes antigen A, IB makes antigen B, and i makes neither; IA and IB are co-dominant and both are dominant to i. Plasma carries antibodies against the ABO antigen a person lacks: group A has anti-B, group B anti-A, group AB neither and group O both. In the Rh system, allele D gives the Rh (D) antigen, so DD and Dd are Rh-positive and dd is Rh-negative; anti-Rh antibodies form only after an Rh-negative person meets Rh-positive cells. O-negative red cells carry no A, B or Rh antigen, so they can be given to anyone; AB-positive plasma has no anti-A, anti-B or anti-Rh, so it can receive any group.

blocks.text: Principle of transfusion in the Rh system

Anti-A and anti-B antibodies are already present in plasma, but Rh-negative people do not naturally have anti-Rh antibodies. If an Rh-negative person receives Rh-positive blood, the body starts making anti-Rh antibodies, which destroy the donated red cells and stay in the body for life.

blocks.title: The true universal donor and recipient
blocks.text: O-negative is the actual universal donor, because it carries no antigen of the ABO system and no Rh antigen. AB-positive is the actual universal recipient, because it has no anti-A, anti-B or anti-Rh antibodies, so it can receive any donor's blood.

blocks.prompt: Why does an Rh-negative person not react to the first transfusion of Rh-positive blood, but can react to a second?
blocks.explanation: There are no natural anti-Rh antibodies, so the first exposure only starts their production; the antibodies then persist for life and attack Rh-positive cells given later.
